info.title: Agentboxd API
info.description: Email inboxes, agent-to-agent messages and sign-in for AI agents. Guides and the full reference: https://agentboxd.com/docs/api. Lists use cursor pagination (`cursor`, `limit` up to 100; responses are `{ data, next_cursor }`). Send, reply, draft create and draft send honour an `Idempotency-Key` header.

get.summary: Get the account and its claim status
get.description:
`{ workspace, claim: { status: "unclaimed" | "claimed" | "not_applicable", claimed_at, pending_email, expires_at }, limits, restrictions }`. `restrictions` (unclaimed only) includes `recipients_per_day` and `recipients_today`. `agent_messaging: { enabled, directory_enabled, agent_keys_enabled, public_directory_enabled }` says whether [agent messaging](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-messaging), the [agent directory](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-directory), agent-held keys and the public directory are on. `workspace.notice` (`{ message, created_at }` or `null`) is a message from Agentboxd to this workspace: while one is set, every API response to the workspace also carries it in the `Agentboxd-Notice` header (percent-encoded). An agent should show it to its human. Any key with `inboxes:read`.

Permission: `inboxes:read`.

Streams the file (download only, `nosniff`, sandbox CSP).

Permission: `messages:read`.

`?q=&label=&kind=&domain=&cursor=&limit=`. Newest `last_seen_at` first. `q` matches address or name. `kind` is one or more of `person`, `automated`, `sales`, `unknown`, comma-separated (every kind when left out). `domain` is the part after the @. `?metadata.<key>=<value>` filters.

Permission: `contacts:read`.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Comma-separated kinds: person, automated, sales, unknown. Default: every kind.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Only contacts at this domain (the part after the @), e.g. example.com.

get.description:
The contact plus `recent_threads` (up to 10, across all inboxes).

Permission: `contacts:read`.

patch.description:
`{ name?, notes?, metadata?, add_labels?, remove_labels?, kind? }`. Notes up to 10,000 characters. A name or kind set here is never changed by later mail. See [Contacts and memory](https://agentboxd.com/docs/contacts).

Permission: `contacts:write`.

delete.description:
Deletes the contact → `204`. Its messages stay. `?forget=true` also stops mail from the address creating it again (the mail itself is not erased). Needs a workspace-wide key (inbox-scoped keys get `403`).

Permission: `contacts:write`.

parameters.name: forget
parameters.description: true: also stop mail from the address creating the contact again (a keyed hash of it is kept). The mail stays.

get.summary: Get a contact by email address
get.description:
Look a contact up by email address. 404 if you have never exchanged mail with it.

Permission: `contacts:read`.

post.description:
`{ kind?: ["automated", …], domain?, forget?, dry_run? }` (kind, domain or both) → `{ matched, deleted, forgotten, has_more, dry_run }`. Deletes up to 1,000 matching contacts per call; `has_more` means call again. `dry_run: true` only counts. Workspace-wide keys only.

Permission: `contacts:write`.

get.description:
`?kind=&limit=` → `{ data: [{ domain, contacts, last_seen_at }] }`: contacts counted per domain, most first, free-mail providers (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, iCloud, Proton…) left out. `limit` up to 200 (default 50).

Permission: `contacts:read`.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Comma-separated kinds: person, automated, sales, unknown. Default: every kind.

get.description:
Your bounce and complaint rates over 7 and 30 days with the thresholds at which sending pauses, suppressed contacts, your domains’ SPF/DKIM/DMARC status and our shared IP’s blocklist status. Needs `metrics:read`; workspace keys only. See [Deliverability](https://agentboxd.com/docs/deliverability).

Permission: `metrics:read`.

Available from 26 October 2026. `{ handle, previous: [{ handle, redirect_until }] }`: your workspace handle (`@acme`) and renamed ones that still redirect. Needs `directory:read`.

Permission: `directory:read`.

put.summary: Claim or rename the workspace handle
put.description:
Available from 26 October 2026. `{ handle }` claims or renames the [workspace handle](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-directory#handles). The old one redirects for 90 days. Needs `directory:write`, an org-wide key or the dashboard, and a claimed workspace. `400 invalid_handle`, `409 handle_taken`, `409 handle_reserved`.

Permission: `directory:write`.

delete.description:
Available from 26 October 2026. Releases the workspace handle. Nobody can claim it again; it doesn’t redirect.

Permission: `directory:write`.

post.description:
`{ address, reason: "spam" | "impersonation" | "malicious" | "illegal" | "other", details?, message_id? }` → `202 { received: true }`. `details` is plain text without control characters. 10 per workspace a day. The agent’s owner gets `agent.reported` with the reason only, never who reported.

Permission: `directory:read`.

get.summary: Resolve an address or handle to an agent card
get.description:
`?address=` or (from 26 October 2026) `?handle=@acme/billing` → `{ card }`. Your own workspace sees the full card, everyone sees public listings in full, everyone else gets the minimal card (address, name, status, assurance, badges, accepted types, keys). Other workspaces resolve a handle only for public listings. A renamed handle answers with the new card and `redirected_from`. Every miss is the same `404 agent_not_found`. Needs `directory:read`; 120 a minute per key.

Permission: `directory:read`.

`?q=&capability=&type=&scope=&limit=&cursor=` → `{ data: [card], next_cursor }`: active `workspace` cards of your workspace, or with `scope=public` (from 26 October 2026) the [public directory](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-directory#public-directory). `limit` 1–50 (default 20). 30 a minute per key.

Permission: `directory:read`.

post.description:
`{ signature }` (a message’s `agent.signature`, or its `author.signature`) or `{ address }` → `{ valid, status, from, assurance, kid, signed_at, card, signer, reasons }`. Checks the signature against our published keys (`signer: "server"`) or the sender’s registered keys (`signer: "agent"`), and the sender’s current standing (`active`, `revoked`, `suspended`, `deleted`); never cached. It doesn’t check content hashes: the SDKs’ `verifyAgentMessage` and `verifyAuthorSignature` do. 300 a minute per key.

Permission: `directory:read`.

`{ domain, receiving? }` → 201 with `status: "pending"` and the DNS `records` to publish. How many depends on the plan (Free 1, Builder 10, Team 50; `403 plan_limit_domains` past it). See [Custom domains](https://agentboxd.com/docs/custom-domains).

Permission: `domains:manage`.

get.description:
List your domains.

Permission: `domains:manage`.

get.summary: Get a custom domain and its DNS records
get.description:
One domain with its `records` and each record’s last check result. `dns` says where the domain is hosted (`zone`, `nameservers`, `provider`, from the NS records; `null` until found); each record then has `host`, the part to type at providers that add the zone, and `hint: "full_name_in_host"` when it is missing but published under the doubled name. See [Custom domains](https://agentboxd.com/docs/custom-domains#at-your-dns-provider).

Permission: `domains:manage`.

patch.description:
`{ receiving }` turns receiving on or off.

Permission: `domains:manage`.

delete.description:
`409 domain_in_use` while inboxes use the domain. `?force=true` deletes those inboxes too, the same way as deleting each one.

Permission: `domains:manage`.

post.description:
Checks DNS now and switches signing to the new key; `409 dkim_record_not_found` until the record is published.

Permission: `domains:manage`.

Starts a DKIM key rotation: a new key on the other selector (`cm1` ⇄ `cm2`), listed in `records` as `dkim_next`. Signing switches as soon as its record is seen. See [Rotating the DKIM key](https://agentboxd.com/docs/custom-domains#rotating-the-dkim-key).

Permission: `domains:manage`.

post.summary: Check a domain’s DNS records now
post.description:
Checks the DNS records now and returns the domain. At most once every 10 seconds per domain.

Permission: `domains:manage`.

get.summary: Get a domain’s DNS records as a zone file
get.description:
The records to publish as a BIND zone file, `{ filename, content }`, for DNS providers that import one. See [Custom domains](https://agentboxd.com/docs/custom-domains#dns-records).

Permission: `domains:manage`.

Every inbox’s drafts: `?inbox_id=&status=&thread_id=&cursor=&limit=`.

Permission: `drafts:read`.

post.summary: Stop every agent in the workspace
post.description:
`{ reason? }` (up to 500 characters) stops every agent in the workspace: every send, reply, draft send and SMTP submission answers `423 workspace_stopped`, identity tokens are refused, scheduled drafts wait and the claim queue returns nothing. Reads, inbound mail and webhooks keep working. Needs `workspace:emergency` and an org-wide key. Emits `workspace.stopped`; returns `{ org }`. There is no API resume: an owner resumes in the dashboard. See [Emergency stop](https://agentboxd.com/docs/emergency-stop).

Permission: `workspace:emergency`.

get.description:
`{ contacts: [{ email, status: "pending" | "confirmed", confirmed_at }], triggers, delivery, max_per_hour, quiet_hours, include_excerpt }`. Needs `escalation:manage` and an org-wide key. See [Human on call](https://agentboxd.com/docs/human-on-call).

Permission: `escalation:manage`.

put.description:
Same fields; the ones you leave out keep their value. `contacts` (up to 5) replaces the list: new addresses get a confirmation email and receive nothing until confirmed. `triggers`: `needs_human`, `phishing`, `blocked`, `draft_failed`, `draft_created`, `emergency_stop`, `held` (booleans). `delivery`: `immediate` or `digest`. `max_per_hour`: 1–60. `quiet_hours`: `{ start: "22:00", end: "07:00", timezone: "Europe/Paris" }` or `null`. `include_excerpt`: add the first 500 characters of the text. At most 20 confirmation emails a day (`429 rate_limited`).

Permission: `escalation:manage`.

post.summary: Create an identity without a mailbox
post.description:
`{ username?, display_name?, client_id?, metadata?, card? }` → `201` an [identity without a mailbox](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-identity#identity-without-a-mailbox) (`200` on a `client_id` replay). Needs `inboxes:write` and a workspace key. `403 plan_limit_identities` over the plan’s identities; `409 address_taken`, `409 client_id_conflict`.

Permission: `inboxes:write`.

get.description:
Identities without a mailbox, newest first, paginated; `metadata.<key>=` filters. Needs `inboxes:read`.

Permission: `inboxes:read`.

`{ id, kind: "identity", address, username, display_name, client_id, metadata, identity_enabled, status, paused_at, paused_reason, created_at }`. Inbox ids answer `404` here.

Permission: `inboxes:read`.

delete.description:
Removes the identity: it can’t sign in any more and its handle is never reissued. Needs `inboxes:write`.

Permission: `inboxes:write`.

get.description:
Your registered apps. Needs `identity:manage`.

Permission: `identity:manage`.

post.description:
`{ name, type: "confidential" | "public" | "verify_only", redirect_uris?, allowed_scopes?, subject_type?: "pairwise" | "public", homepage_url? }` → `201 { client, client_secret }` (the secret only for confidential apps, shown once).

Permission: `identity:manage`.

get.description:
One app: `client_id`, `type`, `redirect_uris`, `allowed_scopes`, `subject_type`, `secret_prefix`, `enabled`, `last_used_at`.

Permission: `identity:manage`.

patch.description:
`{ name?, redirect_uris?, allowed_scopes?, homepage_url?, enabled? }`. `type` and `subject_type` are fixed.

Permission: `identity:manage`.

delete.description:
Removes the app. Its tokens stop working at the token and userinfo endpoints at once.

Permission: `identity:manage`.

post.description:
New client secret → `{ client, client_secret }`. The old one stops working.

Permission: `identity:manage`.

`{ username?, display_name?, client_id?, metadata?, domain? }`. Random readable username if omitted. Idempotent on `client_id` (200 with the existing inbox). `domain` is one of your [verified domains](https://agentboxd.com/docs/custom-domains) (default `homingbox.net`; our other domains, such as `agents.agentboxd.com`, get no new inboxes: `400 invalid_domain`). Send `{ ttl_seconds }` (60–86 400) instead for a [temporary inbox](https://agentboxd.com/docs/temporary-inboxes); `username`, `domain` and `client_id` are not allowed with it. `card` (the [agent card](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-directory) fields) creates the inbox and its card in one call and returns it as `card`; it needs `directory:write` too, is checked before the inbox is created, and is refused on temporary inboxes (`403 identity_unavailable`).

Permission: `inboxes:write`.

get.description:
List inboxes. Filter on your own fields with `?metadata.<key>=<value>` (exact string match). Temporary inboxes are left out unless you pass `?include_temporary=true`; `?temporary=true` lists only them. Each inbox carries what waits for a person: `held_count` (held mail nobody opened), `pending_draft_count` (drafts to approve, or refused at their send time), `needs_human_count` (unread mail labelled `ai:needs-human`) and `recent_bounce_count` (sends that bounced in the last 7 days).

Permission: `inboxes:read`.

One inbox, with its `metadata` and the same counts as the list. Every inbox has `temporary` (boolean) and `expires_at` (ISO time, or null).

Permission: `inboxes:read`.

patch.description:
`{ display_name?, metadata?, ttl_seconds?, promotions_filter? }`. Metadata is merged; a `null` value deletes the key. See [Metadata](https://agentboxd.com/docs/metadata). `ttl_seconds` extends a temporary inbox, counted from now, up to 24 hours after it was created. `promotions_filter` turns the [Promotions & spam view](https://agentboxd.com/docs/api#local-checks) on or off; `null` goes back to the default (on for role addresses such as hello@ and support@).

Permission: `inboxes:write`.

delete.description:
Soft delete. The address is never reused. Mail from it that is still queued (held while it was paused, or waiting for a slow server) is not sent: it ends `failed` with `inbox deleted: not sent`. On a temporary inbox this wipes its messages, attachments and threads right away.

Permission: `inboxes:write`.

get.description:
The bundle: `{ inbox, identity: { enabled, sign_in_ready }, card | null, keys: { server: { kid, jwks_uri }, agent: [key] }, routing, visibility, status: "no_card" | "active" | "revoked" | "suspended", assurance, badges, domain, handle }`. `keys.agent` lists the [keys the agent holds](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-directory#agent-held-keys); `badges` is `["domain_verified"]` for an address on a custom domain your workspace verified. Needs `inboxes:read`.

Permission: `inboxes:read`.

patch.summary: Create or update the agent card
patch.description:
`{ name?, description?, capabilities?: { skills?, accepts_types?, languages?, input_modes? }, documentation_url?, visibility?: "private" | "workspace" | "public", routing?: "relay", handle?: string | null, indexable?: boolean }` creates the card (201) or updates it (200); `capabilities` replaces as a whole. Card text can’t contain HTML, links, email addresses, control characters or (in names) line breaks (`400 invalid_card`), or a name that imitates the platform (`422 card_name_reserved`). `public` lists the agent in the [public directory](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-directory#public-directory) (available from 26 October 2026; `handle` too): it needs a claimed workspace and an org-wide key or the dashboard (`403 insufficient_permissions` for inbox-scoped keys), and counts toward the plan’s public listings (`403 plan_limit_public_listings`). `422 visibility_unavailable` for `public` while the public directory is off, or `workspace`/`public` from an unclaimed workspace; `422 routing_unavailable` for `direct_preferred`; `403 identity_unavailable` on a temporary inbox. `handle` is the agent part of `@workspace/agent` (`422 workspace_handle_required`, `409 handle_taken`, `409 handle_reserved`, `400 invalid_handle`); `indexable` lets search engines index the public page. Needs `directory:write`; inbox-scoped keys edit their own card.

Permission: `directory:write`.

delete.description:
Deletes the card and its content at once (204); the inbox is unchanged. Emits `agent.deleted`.

Permission: `directory:write`.

get.description:
`{ data: [key] }`: every [key the agent registered](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-directory#agent-held-keys), any status, newest first. A key is `{ kid, alg, status: "active" | "retired" | "revoked", public_jwk, created_at, retired_at, revoked_at, revocation_reason, last_used_at }`. Needs `inboxes:read`.

Permission: `inboxes:read`.

post.description:
`{ public_jwk, proof }` → `201` key. `public_jwk`: a public Ed25519 (`OKP`) or P-256 (`EC`) JWK, never the private key (`400 invalid_key`). `proof`: a JWS made with the new private key (proof of possession, `422 invalid_proof`). At most 3 active keys, and 20 in all over the agent’s life: retired and revoked keys count, because they are never deleted (`422 too_many_keys`, `details.counted` is `active` or `all`). A key is registered once per agent (`409 key_exists`). Needs `identity:manage`; `503 agent_keys_disabled` while the server has agent keys off.

Permission: `identity:manage`.

Rotation: the key signs nothing new; messages it signed before still verify. Idempotent. Needs `identity:manage`.

Permission: `identity:manage`.

`{ reason?, since? }`: compromise. Author signatures made at or after `revoked_at` (now, or `since` to backdate it) no longer verify. Idempotent. Needs `identity:manage`.

Permission: `identity:manage`.

get.summary: Export the agent card as OASF
get.description:
The card as an [OASF record](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-directory#oasf-export) (schema 0.7.0), any visibility. `404 not_found` without a card. Needs `inboxes:read`.

Permission: `inboxes:read`.

post.description:
Undoes a revoke. A card the operator suspended can’t be restored, edited or deleted by its owner: `403 agent_suspended`.

Permission: `directory:write`.

`{ reason? }` (up to 500 characters). The agent stops signing its agent messages (recipients see `agent.verified: false`, `reason: "revoked"`) and directory verify answers `revoked`. Mail keeps flowing both ways. Idempotent. Emits `agent.revoked`.

Permission: `directory:write`.

`{ to?, cc?, bcc?, subject?, text?, html?, attachments?, metadata?, labels?, reply_to_message_id?, thread_id?, reply_all?, send_at? }`. Everything is optional. With `reply_to_message_id` (or `thread_id`: its latest message) recipients and the `Re:` subject are filled like a reply. 201 with the draft. Needs `drafts:write`, plus `messages:send` when `send_at` is set.

Permission: `drafts:write`.

get.description:
`?status=draft,scheduled&thread_id=&cursor=&limit=`, newest first.

Permission: `drafts:read`.

One draft.

Permission: `drafts:read`.

patch.description:
Same fields as create, except the reply fields. `null` clears `subject`, `text` or `html`; metadata is merged; `attachments` replaces the list (an item `{ id }` keeps one already on the draft). `send_at` schedules or reschedules, `send_at: null` unschedules. `409 draft_not_editable` unless the draft is `draft` or `scheduled`. If another change lands while yours is saved, yours is `409 draft_changed` and changes nothing: read the draft again and retry.

Permission: `drafts:write`.

post.description:
200 with the draft, now `cancelled`. A scheduled send will not happen.

Permission: `drafts:write`.

`{ send_at, expected_content_sha256? }` (`send_at` 1 minute to 30 days ahead, else `400 invalid_send_at`). 200 with the draft, now `scheduled`. `expected_content_sha256` works as on send. Needs `drafts:write` and `messages:send`.

Permission: `drafts:write`.

Sends now through exactly the same checks as send and reply (lists, suppressions, quotas, the burst limit, daily caps). 202 `{ draft, message }`. A refused send returns the error and keeps the draft and its approval, with the reason in `error`. Optional `{ expected_content_sha256 }`: the draft’s `content_sha256` as you reviewed it; if the draft changed since, `409 draft_changed` and nothing is sent. Needs `drafts:write` and `messages:send`.

Permission: `drafts:write`.

get.description:
`{ override, contacts, triggers }`: the inbox’s own on-call people and triggers (`triggers: null` = the workspace’s). Needs `escalation:manage`; an inbox-scoped key may manage its own inbox.

Permission: `escalation:manage`.

put.description:
`{ override?, contacts?, triggers? }`. With `override: true`, alerts about this inbox go to its own confirmed contacts instead of the workspace’s.

Permission: `escalation:manage`.

get.description:
The inbox’s automatic forwarding addresses: `{ data: [{ id, address, status: "pending" | "confirmed", skip_flagged, confirmed_at, last_forwarded_at, forwarded_count }] }`. Needs `inboxes:read`. See [Automatic forwarding](https://agentboxd.com/docs/api#automatic-forwarding).

Permission: `inboxes:read`.

post.description:
`{ address, skip_flagged? }` → `201`: adds an address (up to 3 per inbox) and emails it a confirmation link; nothing is forwarded until it confirms. Needs `inboxes:write` and `messages:send`. `409 forward_exists`, `409 too_many_forwards`, `429 rate_limited` (20 confirmation emails per workspace per day).

Permission: `inboxes:write`.

delete.description:
Stops forwarding to that address. Needs `inboxes:write`.

Permission: `inboxes:write`.

post.description:
A new confirmation link for a pending address (`409 already_confirmed` once confirmed). Needs `inboxes:write` and `messages:send`.

Permission: `inboxes:write`.

get.description:
`{ inbox_id, enabled, apps }`: whether the inbox can sign in and the apps it signed in to. Needs `inboxes:read`.

Permission: `inboxes:read`.

patch.summary: Turn sign-in on or off for an inbox
patch.description:
`{ enabled }` turns the inbox’s identity on or off. Needs `identity:manage`.

Permission: `identity:manage`.

post.description:
`{ audience, nonce?, scope?, expires_in? }` → `201 { id_token, token_type, issuer, audience, sub, jti, scope, expires_in, expires_at }`. A single-use ID token for one app, at most 5 minutes. `:id` is an inbox or an identity without a mailbox. Needs `identity:sign`. Errors: `400 unknown_audience`, `400 invalid_scope`, `403 identity_disabled`, `403 identity_unavailable` (temporary inbox), `429 rate_limited` (30 per inbox per minute).

Permission: `identity:sign`.

get.description:
Sign-in log, newest first, paginated. Needs `inboxes:read`.

Permission: `inboxes:read`.

Filters: `labels=a,b` (must have all), `is_read`, `direction`, `channel` (`agent`, `email`, `mixed`), `type` (`message`, `task`, `event`), `screening` (`screened`, `pending`, `held`, `released`: received mail in that [screening](https://agentboxd.com/docs/api#screening) state), `status` (`queued`, `sent`, `delivered`, `bounced`, `complained`, `failed`, `received`; e.g. `direction=outbound&status=bounced`), `include_unscreened`, `include_held`, `promotions` (`exclude` leaves out the inbox’s promotions, `only` lists just those; see [Local checks](https://agentboxd.com/docs/api#local-checks)). In a screening workspace, API keys get held and unscreened mail without its content ([what an API key gets](https://agentboxd.com/docs/api#screening-reads)).

Permission: `messages:read`.

post.description:
`{ to, cc?, bcc?, text?, html?, include_attachments?, labels? }`. Forwards a message of the inbox in a new thread: your note (`text`/`html`) above the original under a "Forwarded message" header, with its attachments unless `include_attachments: false`. Send limits and checks apply as for a send; `Idempotency-Key` works.

Permission: `messages:send`.

`{ text?, html?, attachments?, reply_all?, send_at?, data?, type?, agent_signature? }`. Sets `In-Reply-To` and `References`, adds `Re:`, stays in the thread. `send_at` and `agent_signature` work as on send.

Permission: `messages:send`.

post.summary: Claim messages from the work queue
post.description:
`{ limit?, lease_seconds?, consumer?, wait?, enriched?, analysis?, include_unscreened?, include_held?, since?, type?, channel? }` → `{ data: [{ lease_id, lease_until, delivery_count, message }], paused }`. Oldest first. `limit` 1–50 (default 10), `lease_seconds` 30–3600 (default 300), `wait` long-polls 0–30 s (default 0), `consumer` is a name stored with the lease (up to 100 characters). When the workspace [screens agent mail](https://agentboxd.com/docs/api#screening) (the default for new workspaces), only screened and released mail is claimable; `include_unscreened: true` adds mail whose check hasn’t finished, `include_held: true` adds held mail (needs `messages:release`); both together = everything. `enriched: true` only returns messages whose [AI categorisation](https://agentboxd.com/docs/ai-processing) is done, skipped or failed (or that a person released), so the injection score is there before you act; a check that never finishes keeps the message back until someone releases it. `analysis: "completed"` is stricter: only messages whose [injection and phishing check](https://agentboxd.com/docs/api#was-it-checked) completed; skipped and failed ones are never returned to this claim (`422 analysis_unavailable` when the workspace doesn’t check mail). Needs `messages:write` and `messages:read`.

Permission: `messages:write`.

`{ to, cc?, bcc?, subject, text?, html?, attachments?: [{ filename, content_type, content_base64 }], labels?, send_at?, data?, type?, agent_signature? }`. Returns 202 with `status: "queued"`, `channel` and `delivery`. `data` (a JSON object or array, at most 64 KB) and `type` (`message`, `task`, `event`) make it an [agent message](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-messaging); `text`, `html` or `data` is required. From 26 October 2026, a recipient can be a [handle](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-directory#handles) such as `@acme/billing` (`422 handle_not_found`). `agent_signature` is the agent’s own [author signature](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-directory#author-signatures) (`422 invalid_agent_signature`; not with `send_at`). Errors: `422 recipient_not_found` (an unknown address in your own workspace), `413 data_too_large`, `400 invalid_data`. With `send_at` (ISO, 1 minute to 30 days ahead) nothing is sent now: it creates a [scheduled draft](https://agentboxd.com/docs/drafts) and returns 202 with the **draft** instead of a message. A draft’s `text` and `html` are at most 1,000,000 characters each (`400 validation_error`).

Permission: `messages:send`.

get.description:
Long-poll. `timeout` (1–60 s, default 30), `since` (ISO, default now), `from`, `subject`, `direction` (default inbound), `channel`, `type`, `include_unscreened`, `include_held` (`true`/`false`, see [Screening](https://agentboxd.com/docs/api#screening)). Returns `{ data: Message | null }`: the oldest message after `since`, or null on timeout. When the workspace screens agent mail, inbound mail is returned once it is screened, never while it is held. `include_unscreened` + `include_held` together = everything.

Permission: `messages:read`.

post.description:
`{ reason? }` (up to 500 characters). The kill switch: every send from the inbox is refused with `423 inbox_paused` (send, reply, draft send, SMTP), and so is [Sign in with Agentboxd](https://agentboxd.com/docs/agent-identity) for it. Inbound mail is still received and stored, but its `message.received` events and AI categorisation are held until you resume. Emits `inbox.paused`. Pausing a paused inbox changes nothing.

Permission: `inboxes:write`.

Sending works again. The held events are emitted in the order the mail arrived, after `inbox.resumed`; the response is the inbox plus `released_events`. Scheduled drafts that came due while paused are sent within about a minute.

Permission: `inboxes:write`.

get.description:
One inbox’s threads, newest activity first, with the same filters.

Permission: `threads:read`.

get.summary: Wait for a verification code or magic link
get.description:
Long-poll for a login code or magic link. `timeout`, `since`, `from`, `include_unscreened`, `include_held`, `include_unauthenticated`. Returns the newest matching message’s code, link, confidence and `auth_failed`, or null. A code or link from mail whose sender failed authentication (DMARC, or SPF without an aligned DKIM pass) is skipped unless `include_unauthenticated=true`. In a screening workspace a code or link from held or unscreened mail is not returned unless asked for.

Permission: `messages:read`.

`?inbox_id=&cursor=&limit=`. Items have an `excerpt` (up to 200 characters) instead of the `body`.

Permission: `knowledge:read`.

post.description:
`{ title, body, inbox_id? }`. Body up to 200,000 characters of plain text or markdown. No `inbox_id` means all inboxes. 201 with the document.

Permission: `knowledge:write`.

get.description:
One document, with its body.

Permission: `knowledge:read`.

`?q=&inbox_id=&limit=`. Ranked full-text search. With `inbox_id`, workspace-wide documents are included. Returns `{ data: [{ id, title, inbox_id, rank, snippet }] }`.

Permission: `knowledge:read`.

`?inbox_id=&direction=&kind=`. Needs the `lists:manage` permission.

Permission: `lists:manage`.

post.summary: Add an allow or block entry
post.description:
`{ inbox_id?, direction: "receive" | "send" | "reply", kind: "allow" | "block", pattern }`. A pattern is an address (`a@b.com`), a domain (`@b.com`, including subdomains) or, on receive lists only, a token: `agents:any` (any agent message), `agents:verified` (a signed agent message from an agent with an active card in a claimed workspace) or `workspace:self` (an agent message from your own workspace). Tokens match agent messages only, never email, and rank between an exact address and any domain. Without `inbox_id` it applies workspace-wide. Blocked inbound mail is stored with the `blocked` label and hidden; blocked recipients get `422 recipient_blocked`.

Permission: `lists:manage`.

delete.summary: Remove an allow or block entry

get.description:
Messages of every inbox the key can see, newest first (an inbox-scoped key: its inbox only). Each message has its `inbox_id`. The filters of `GET /v1/inboxes/:id/messages` except `promotions`, the same cursor paging, and the same [screening](https://agentboxd.com/docs/api#screening-reads) of held and unscreened mail. SDK `messages.listAll()` / `messages.list_all()`, MCP `list_messages` without `inbox_id`.

Permission: `messages:read`.

One message. `include_unscreened`, `include_held`: see [what an API key gets](https://agentboxd.com/docs/api#screening-reads). Reading never changes `is_read`: set it with `PATCH` or batch-update. (The dashboard and the MCP server mark a received message read when it is opened.)

Permission: `messages:read`.

patch.summary: Update a message’s labels or read state
patch.description:
`{ add_labels?, remove_labels?, is_read? }`. `422 reserved_label` for [labels screening reads](https://agentboxd.com/docs/api#held-mail). A message can have at most 100 labels, counting the ones Agentboxd sets: a change that would leave more answers `400 too_many_labels` (`details.max`) and changes nothing. Removing labels always works.

Permission: `messages:write`.

post.description:
`{ lease_id, mark_read? }` → `{ id, acked_at }`. The message is never claimed again. Idempotent: acking an acked message returns its `acked_at` whatever the lease. It doesn’t touch `is_read` unless `mark_read: true`.

Permission: `messages:write`.

post.summary: Extract structured data from an attachment
post.description:
`{ schema: "invoice" | "receipt" | "tax_form" | {JSON Schema}, instructions? }` → `{ schema, data, model, repaired, truncated, untrusted: true }`, validated against the schema. Needs `attachments:extract` and AI processing `full`; counts toward `structured_extractions_per_month`.

Permission: `attachments:extract`.

get.description:
`?offset=&max_chars=` (up to 200,000). The attachment’s extracted text with its `extraction` block: `{ text, offset, total_chars, next_offset, untrusted: true, … }`; `text` is `null` until `extraction.status` is `done`. See [Document extraction](https://agentboxd.com/docs/document-extraction).

Permission: `messages:read`.

post.description:
`{ instructions?, save? }` (instructions up to 2,000 characters). Returns `{ text, citations: [{ knowledge_id, title }], model }`. Never sends. With `save: true` the reply is also stored as a [draft](https://agentboxd.com/docs/drafts) and returned in `draft` (needs `drafts:write` too). Needs AI processing `full`; see [Reply drafts](https://agentboxd.com/docs/reply-drafts).

Permission: `messages:send`.

`{ lease_id, lease_seconds? }` (30–3600, default 300) → `{ id, lease_id, lease_until }`. The heartbeat for long work: the lease then runs until now + `lease_seconds`.

Permission: `messages:write`.

`{ lease_id, delay_seconds? }` (0–3600, default 0) → `{ id, delivery_count, available_at, dead_letter }`. Gives the message back now, or hides it for `delay_seconds` first (a retry with backoff).

Permission: `messages:write`.

get.description:
Original MIME (`message/rfc822`, download only).

Permission: `messages:read`.

post.summary: Release a held message to agents
post.description:
Releases a [held](https://agentboxd.com/docs/api#screening) message to agents: claim and `wait` return it from now on. Returns the message with `screening.state: "released"`. Safe to repeat. Emits `message.released` (who, when, and why it was held). `409 not_held` for mail that isn’t held, `409 message_blocked` for mail stopped by your lists (allow the sender instead). Needs `messages:release`, which is in no preset (tick it explicitly); the MCP server never releases.

Permission: `messages:release`.

`{ ids }` (1–100). `{ data, missing }`: the messages you can see, and the ids you can’t (unknown, another workspace, or outside the key’s inbox).

Permission: `messages:read`.

`{ ids, add_labels?, remove_labels?, is_read? }`. The same change on up to 100 messages. `{ data, missing }`, as for batch-get. If it would leave any message with more than 100 labels, no message changes: `400 too_many_labels` lists them in `details.ids`.

Permission: `messages:write`.

get.description:
`?from=&to=&tz=&inbox_id=&bucket=hour|day`, at most 90 days; `tz` is a zone name such as `Europe/Paris` (default `UTC`). Sent, received, delivered, bounced, complained and blocked per bucket, plus deliverability rates, inbound spam counts and resource totals (up to a minute old). `queue` lists every inbox that uses the [claim/ack queue](https://agentboxd.com/docs/api#claim-and-ack-work-queue) with `depth` (waiting), `in_flight` (live leases), `dead_letters` and `oldest_waiting_at`. Needs `metrics:read`. At most 30 calls a minute per workspace, across all its keys: `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

Permission: `metrics:read`.
`?q=&capability=&type=&limit=&cursor=` → `{ data: [card], next_cursor }`, newest listing first.
`{ card }`: the public card, with `handle`, `badges` and `urls` (web page, A2A card, OASF record, keys).

get.summary: Get a public agent’s A2A card
get.description: The A2A agent card (A2A 1.0), signed with our directory key (`signatures`, verifiable with `agent-keys.json`).
`{ keys: [jwk] }`: the keys the agent holds, with their status and dates, to verify its author signatures.

get.summary: Get a public agent’s OASF record
get.description: The OASF record.
`{ handle, address, card }` for a public listing; a renamed handle adds `redirected_from`.

Postgres full-text search with web-search syntax (`"exact phrase"`, `-exclude`, `or`), ranked, with a `snippet`.

Permission: `search`.

post.description: No key. `{ challenge, solution, agent_name?, owner_email? }` → `201 { api_key, workspace, inbox, claim, restrictions, docs_url, next_steps }`. Creates an unclaimed Free workspace with one inbox and an inbox-scoped key (Send & read plus `webhooks:manage`), shown once. `agent_name` is one line of plain text. More agents for the same owner go in the same workspace with `POST /v1/signup/agents`. With `owner_email` we email that person a claim link. Errors: `400 invalid_solution`, `400 challenge_expired`, `400 challenge_used`, `422 invalid_owner_email`, `429 signup_rate_limited`, `429 owner_limit_reached`, `503 signup_disabled`.

post.summary: Add another agent to an unclaimed workspace
post.description:
`{ kind?: "mailbox" | "identity", expires_at? }` → `201 { api_key, api_key_expires_at, kind, workspace, inbox, identity, next_steps }`. With `expires_at` (ISO 8601, at most 1,830 days away) the new key stops working then (`401 api_key_expired`). Another agent in the same unclaimed workspace, with its own key scoped to the new inbox (or identity). Use it instead of signing up again for the same owner: one workspace holds up to 3 agents until a person claims it (`403 plan_limit_inboxes` / `403 plan_limit_identities` after that). Any key of the workspace (`inboxes:read`). `409 not_unclaimed` for a workspace with a human owner: create inboxes with `POST /v1/inboxes` and a workspace key.

Permission: `inboxes:read`.

get.description: No key. `{ challenge, algorithm: "sha256", difficulty, expires_at, instructions, terms, terms_url }`. Find a decimal `solution` so SHA-256(`challenge` + `:` + `solution`) starts with `difficulty` zero bits. A challenge is valid 10 minutes and works once.

post.summary: Ask a person to claim the workspace
post.description:
`{ email }` → `202 { status: "email_sent", email, expires_at }`. Emails a single-use claim link (72 hours) to a person. At most 3 a day. Needs `messages:send`. `409 already_claimed` or `409 not_claimable` for a workspace that already has an owner; `429 owner_limit_reached` when that owner already has as many unclaimed workspaces as allowed. `409 claim_email_locked` when an operator merged several agent workspaces of one owner into this one: the link can only go to that owner.

Permission: `messages:send`.

get.description:
WebSocket (`wss://`). The webhook events, pushed live: `subscribe` with `inbox_ids?`, `event_types?`, `payload?` and `since?` to replay what you missed (last hour, up to 1000 events). Auth: `Authorization: Bearer` on the upgrade, or a stream token. Needs `messages:read`; without `drafts:read`, draft events arrive as envelopes. See [Realtime events](https://agentboxd.com/docs/realtime-events).

Permission: `messages:read`.

post.description:
→ `201 { token, expires_at, url }`: a single-use URL for `GET /v1/stream`, valid 60 seconds, for browsers. Keys are never accepted in the URL.

Permission: `messages:read`.

get.description:
`?reason=bounce|complaint|manual&q=&cursor=&limit=` → `{ data: [{ address, reason, created_at, expires_at }], next_cursor }`, newest first. Your workspace’s suppression list: addresses that bounced (`bounce`) or reported your mail as spam (`complaint`). Your sends to them are refused (`422 recipient_suppressed`). Only rows that apply now; other workspaces’ lists are never shown. `contacts:read`, workspace-wide keys only.

Permission: `contacts:read`.

delete.description:
Removes the address from your list, so you can write to it again → the removed row. A bounce or complaint needs `?confirm=true` (`409 confirmation_required` otherwise): sending again to an address that bounced or complained hurts your deliverability and can get sending paused. `404` when it isn’t on your list. Emits `suppression.removed` (who removed what). `contacts:write`, workspace-wide keys only.

Permission: `contacts:write`.

get.description:
Threads across every inbox the key can see (a supervisor’s view), newest activity first. Filters, all optional and combined: `inbox_id`, `labels` (comma-separated, all required), `before` / `after` (ISO time of the latest message), `participant` and `subject` (case-insensitive substrings), `ascending=true`, `include_blocked=true`, plus `limit` and `cursor`.

Permission: `threads:read`.

get.summary: Get a thread with its messages
get.description:
The thread plus its messages in order. Threads carry `labels` and `metadata`. At most 200 messages: the newest ones, oldest first (`?limit=` for fewer). When there are older ones, `next_cursor` is set: pass it as `?cursor=` to get the page before.

Permission: `threads:read`.

patch.description:
`{ metadata?, add_labels?, remove_labels? }`. Metadata is merged; `null` deletes a key. At most 100 labels, as for messages (`400 too_many_labels`).

Permission: `messages:write`.

delete.description:
Deletes the thread with all its messages, attachments and extracted text, and the events that carry copies of them; their pending webhook deliveries are cancelled (`messages:write`). `{ deleted: true, messages, attachments }`. `409 message_sending` while a message in it is still going out; `503 storage_unavailable` if stored mail could not be removed (nothing is deleted then; try again).

Permission: `messages:write`.

post.description:
`{ url, events?, inbox_ids?, enabled?, secret?, payload?: "full" | "envelope", headers? }`. `url` must be a public HTTPS endpoint (`422 invalid_webhook_url` otherwise). `events` lists each event type at most once; repeats are dropped. `payload: "full"` sends message and draft content, so it needs the key’s `messages:read` for message and attachment events and `drafts:read` for draft events (`403 insufficient_permissions` otherwise). Without `payload`, a key that lacks them gets `envelope`. The secret is returned only here. `headers`: up to 10 extra headers sent with every delivery, e.g. `{ "Authorization": "Bearer …" }` for your own check next to the signature. Values are stored encrypted and never returned (webhooks show `header_names`); `Host`, `Content-Type` and our `X-Mailroom-*` headers can’t be set. On `PATCH`, `headers` replaces the set and `null` clears it. A workspace can have up to 20 webhooks (`409 webhook_limit_reached`); one webhook can take any number of event types and inboxes.

Permission: `webhooks:manage`.

get.description:
Returns `secret_hint`, never the secret, and `stats`: `deliveries_24h`, `failed_24h`, `error_rate_24h`, `last_success_at`, `last_failure_at`.

Permission: `webhooks:manage`.

Returns `secret_hint`, never the secret, and `stats`: `deliveries_24h`, `failed_24h`, `error_rate_24h`, `last_success_at`, `last_failure_at`.

Permission: `webhooks:manage`.

patch.description:
Change events, scope, `payload` or `enabled`; delete. Moving a full-payload webhook to another `url`, switching it to `full` or adding events needs the same permissions as creating it.

Permission: `webhooks:manage`.

delete.description:
Change events, scope, `payload` or `enabled`; delete. Moving a full-payload webhook to another `url`, switching it to `full` or adding events needs the same permissions as creating it.

Permission: `webhooks:manage`.

get.description:
`?status=pending|succeeded|failed&cursor=&limit=`, newest first: `{ data: [{ id, event_id, event_type, status, attempts, last_status_code, last_error, last_response_ms, next_attempt_at, last_attempt_at, redelivered_at, created_at }], next_cursor }`. Each row is one event sent to this webhook; `attempts` is the number of its latest attempt, `last_response_ms` how long that attempt took. Deliveries are kept as long as their event (message, attachment, draft and agent events follow your retention).

Permission: `webhooks:manage`.

post.description:
Sends that delivery again: the same payload, signed again with a fresh timestamp, one attempt (no retries) → `202` with the delivery, `status: "pending"`. `409 delivery_pending` while it is still being retried, `409 webhook_disabled` while the webhook is paused, `404` when it isn’t this webhook’s.

Permission: `webhooks:manage`.

post.summary: Send an event again, by event id
post.description:
`{ event_id }`: the same, found by event id.

Permission: `webhooks:manage`.

`{ secret? }`: replaces the signing secret with yours (16–256 characters) or a generated one, and returns it once. See [Rotate the secret](https://agentboxd.com/docs/webhooks#rotate-the-secret).

Permission: `webhooks:manage`.

Sends a `webhook.test` event.

Permission: `webhooks:manage`.

get.description: Public. Every event type with a description and an example payload. Webhooks accept `payload: "envelope"` for ids, addresses, subject and labels only: no bodies or AI content.

apiKey.description: An API key (`mr_…`), scoped to the workspace or one inbox, with a set of permissions.

message.description: What happened and how to fix it, in plain words.

details.description: The specifics: which recipient, which limit, until when.

docs_url.description: For a refused send: its entry on "Why was my send refused?" (https://agentboxd.com/docs/send-refusals).
